title: Mum's Chicken Goulash (Hungarian-style tomato soup)
ingredients: 2 kg chicken pieces (bone-in or boneless, as preferred)
4–5 bacon stock cubes (or substitute with chicken stock cubes if unavailable)
1 can water (for each can of soup)
method: Heat a large pot or Dutch oven over medium heat with a drizzle of oil.
Add the diced onions and sauté until softened and lightly golden.
Pour in the two cans of tomato soup.
Fill each empty can with water and add to the pot (2 cans of water in total).
Stir well to combine. If you prefer a creamier texture, add the milk at this stage.
Add the chicken pieces, green capsicum slices, cubed potatoes, and stock cubes.
Stir to ensure the ingredients are evenly distributed.
Bring the mixture to a boil over medium-high heat.
Reduce the heat to low, cover, and let it simmer gently for 40 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Add the peas in the last 10 minutes if using.
Taste the goulash and adjust seasoning as needed.
Serve hot in bowls, accompanied by crusty bread or over buttered noodles for a complete meal.
timing: 5:30 PM - Start prepping vegetables and chicken | 5:45 PM - Sauté onions in the pot | 5:50 PM - Add soup, water, and milk to the pot | 5:55 PM - Add chicken, capsicum, potatoes, and stock cubes. Bring to boil | 6:00 PM - Reduce heat, cover, and simmer for 40 minutes | 6:20 PM - Add peas (if using). Stir and adjust seasoning | 6:25 PM - Turn off heat. Let the goulash rest for 5 minutes | 6:30 PM - Serve and enjoy!
summary: Family chicken-and-capsicum stew in tomato soup — not a classic beef goulash.
notes: Title says goulash for family nostalgia; it is chicken pieces simmered in tomato soup with capsicum and potato.

title: Long-Slow Instant Pot Beef Bourguignon
cookTime: 8–10 hr Low + overnight fridge + 20–30 min reduce
ingredients: 1 kg beef chuck, cut into 4–5 cm chunks, patted dry
100g bacon or speck, cut into lardons
400ml red wine you would drink (Pinot, Shiraz or Cab blend)
Oil only if the pot looks dry
8–12 shallots, peeled and halved if large (Day 2)
method: DAY 1 — Instant Pot Sauté Normal. Cook the bacon until the fat renders and it browns. Lift the bacon out. Leave the fat in the pot.
Sear the chuck in two batches, 2–3 min a side. Do not crowd. Lift out with the bacon.
If the bottom is sticky, splash of wine or stock and scrape clean.
Onion and carrot 4–5 min. Garlic 1 min. Tomato paste 1 min.
Pour in the wine. Scrape hard. Let it bubble 2–3 min so it does not taste raw.
Return beef and bacon. Add stock, bay, thyme and pepper. Liquid should come about two-thirds up the meat. Go easy on salt — bacon is salty.
Cancel Sauté. Slow Cook Low, lid on venting (or glass lid). Cook 8–10 hours. 9–10 is the sweet spot. Keep Warm for 1–2 hours after is OK.
Cool 20–30 minutes. Fridge overnight (8–12 hours is enough). Do not reduce yet. Do not add mushrooms or shallots yet.
DAY 2 — Scoop off the solid fat. Bin most of it. Fish out the bay and thyme stalks.
Instant Pot Sauté Normal, lid off. Reduce 15–25 minutes, stirring, until it is a glossy gravy that coats a spoon. Stay saucy — not rendang-dry. Drop to Less if it catches.
Optional: sprinkle in the flour, stir 1 minute, then keep reducing.
In a frypan, brown mushrooms and shallots in butter. They need their own colour.
Stir mushrooms and shallots into the pot for the last 5–10 minutes.
Taste: salt, pepper, a splash of wine if it is flat. Rest 10 minutes. Parsley. Serve with mash, buttered noodles or bread.
timing: Day 1: bacon, sear and build sauce ~25 min, Slow Cook Low 8–10 hours lid on venting, optional Keep Warm 1–2 hours, cool, fridge overnight. Day 2: skim fat, Sauté reduce 15–25 min to glossy gravy, brown mushrooms and shallots separately, fold in 5–10 min, rest 10 min.
recommendedDrinks: Same red wine used in the pot
summary: Bourguignon in the long-slow rendang style: sear first, no pressure, 8–10 hr Low, overnight fridge, then a saucy Sauté reduce. Mushrooms and shallots go in on day 2.
notes: No pressure cook. Long Slow Cook Low plus fridge rest is the point.
Use wine you would drink. Cheap cooking wine stays sharp.
Stop at glossy gravy, not a dry coat.
Brown mushrooms and shallots on day 2 so they do not turn to mush.
